next_action: P7 cell 2 (D22) is COMPLETE: the unshared MTP head (mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf) with a 1-token draft does not beat M1 on either t/s (22.6316 vs 28.6646, -21.03% raw) or first-position acceptance (0.7832 vs 0.7851, no gain). The raw t/s drop is an isolated system anomaly on 2 of 16 cases (L07/L08@ctx32k: decode 3-4x slower, free RAM below 4 GB, GPU power collapsed to 81W vs 135W at equal or higher clock -- a transport-stall signature, not thermal, not isolated experimentally); depurated t/s is 29.04 (+1.3%, within single-replica noise) but depurated acceptance stays at 0.7797, still below 0.7851 -- the verdict does not change even in the most favorable case. Fingerprints 18/18 identical to M1 (verification correctness confirmed). VRAM +302 MiB, RAM +1.03 GB. M5 not run (neither trigger condition met). Decision D23: the unshared head is not adopted -- draft accuracy is not improved by swapping the available head. New risk R-RAM: with the MTP head on and 32k context, free RAM drops to ~4-5 GB, and below 4 GB decode collapses (transport stall, not thermal); every future preset must log minimum free RAM during the run, and a cell with a minimum below 4 GB is not a clean speed measurement. Next: P7 cell 3 (cost of the verify row, 16.6 ms: 6.6 mmvq + 6.4 transfers) is in preparation, pending the GitHub MTP-acceptance reconnaissance (docs/porto/RICOGNIZIONE_MTP_ACCETTAZIONE_14_SETTEMBRE.md, being written by another agent -- do not create it from this task). The cache-hit-gap front (41% vs 75%) is still NOT the P7 front (D19).

phases.alternative_start: documented closure of the CPU route after an inconclusive or negative matched confirmation (D18, exercised 9/14)

decisions_added.summary: Token budgets raised to 1024 (screening) / 1536 (confirmation) for free-form cases, 768 for structured-quality and long-context cases, replacing the protocol's 512/768.

Baseline variability is measured on the solo_libero profile (8 free-form cases, short context and 32k) with three alternating-order A=A pairs, plus a single full screening block as reference and as a proof of the 131k schema.
Deterministic CPU-miss ordering for P3: first misses in unique-index order, as proposed by the P1 contract; alternative orderings deferred to P4.

User decision, 9/14, binding: run candidate B first against the already-known reference; if B shows the advantage, skip A; if not, also run A to separate a general regression from one specific to the candidate. No long control batteries without a ready candidate. Stopped the D12 baseline-variability measurement after three blocks (two complete + one interrupted); the full screening block is not run. Closed baseline reference for P3/P4: 24.44 t/s on the free set.

With --reasoning on and the screening token budget, 14 of 16 free-form cases finish on length with an empty final text (only L04@corto and L04@ctx32k reach stop). Speed measurement stays valid; the free-form quality rubric is not applicable in screening and is deferred to confirmation (P6) with a 3072 budget or run-to-stop.

Default of LLAMA_MOE_CPU_THREADS moved from 4 to 2, with pool affinity kept away from the server thread that enqueues to the GPU. P4 cell 1 confirms P2's R7: the pool is pinned from core 0 on an 8-physical-core machine running the server at -t 16, so a 4-thread pool shares a core with the GPU-enqueue thread. D03 revised: 4/6 core threads are no longer candidates (6 threads costs +7.7 ms/token).

The CPU route does not close after P4 cell 1; it continues with cell 2, 'light plumbing and extension': one host node per layer instead of two, merge guard without a PCIe read, thread affinity; then 8/24/47 layers, candidate B first, A only if needed (D14). Exit criterion unchanged: +5% on the free set for adoption, <3% for closure.

CPU route CLOSED (9/14). The orchestrator stopped P4 cell 2 right after the 24-layer verification run, before the 24-layer free block and any 47-layer run: the numbers already collected settle the verdict. Light plumbing cuts per-layer cost 47% (112.4->59.1 us) but stays 6.6% of decode at 47 layers, and measured free-set t/s is -1.6% at 8 layers (clean measurement) and -5.9% at 24 layers (verification run, counters on but same direction and larger), both under the plan's <3% closure threshold, with the loss growing rather than shrinking with scale. Result preserved: P3+P4 patches stay on D:\ds4_work\p3_work, off by default (LLAMA_MOE_CPU=0); bin_prod never touched. P5/P6 become not applicable; move to P7.

The cache-hit gap (41% vs 75%) is NOT an open front. Falsified by Codex on 9/13: real hit rate 75.55% (75.55% on steps past 64 per cache, 74.51% on the full trace), measured directly and confirmed against the simulator on 36,913 GPU plans with zero differences; the 41% came from an indirect PCIe-traffic estimate that overstated misses. On 9/14 the front was mistakenly reopened in this registry's status/next-action text without reading RIPRESA_CACHE_13_SETTEMBRE_CODEX.md, and closed within about an hour with no runs produced. Binding rule: before opening or reopening a front already touched in a prior session, read the relevant *_CODEX.md reports.

P7 cell 1 = MTP draft length (speculation). Chosen after the 9/13 Codex chat digest and VERSO_50_TPS_400_PREFILL_13_SETTEMBRE_CODEX.md (decode profile: expert upload 24.5%, Q6_K 23%, IQ2_S 9.9%, attention 7.9%; MTP acceptance 70-75% with a 1-token draft; n-grams already falsified as a general setting, they only help copy-tasks and hurt free-form prose). Protocol per D14: run M2 (2-token draft) first against the already-known reference M1 (1-token draft, current production regime); run M3 (3-token draft) only if M2 beats M1. solo_libero profile, original experimental binaries, no code changes in this cell. Adoption threshold +5% on the free set, same criterion as D17 for P4.

New reference with speculation on this bench: 28.66 t/s (M1, 1-token MTP draft, shared Q8_0 head, LLAMA_MTP_LIGHT=1). Measured in P7 cell 1: 28.6646 t/s vs 24.4344 t/s with MTP off (+17.31%), 0.785 acceptance, 1.788 tokens/pass, +5.60% on the iso-text 32k subset. Codex's 27.26 t/s from 9/13 stays historical: different preset, budget, and bench, does not replace this reference.

The MTP draft does not get lengthened from 1 to 2 tokens: the lever is draft accuracy or the cost of the verify row, not length. M2 (2-token draft) loses 4.05% against M1 (-4.74% on the iso-text 32k subset): the second draft position costs 22.08 ms (11.1 head + 16.6 third verify row, ~6.6 ms mmvq + ~6.4 ms transfers per the 9/10 measurement) and yields only 0.535 tokens, below the 0.633 break-even (measured 0.553); M3 not runnable (3-row guards). Cell 2 opened accordingly: unshared MTP head (mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf), draft 1 first (D14), draft 2 only if second-position acceptance clears 0.633.

The unshared MTP head is not adopted (P7 cell 2, COMPLETE 9/14, commit 07b07a1). M4 (unshared head, 1-token draft) beats M1 on neither t/s (22.6316 vs 28.6646, -21.03% raw) nor first-position acceptance (0.7832 vs 0.7851, no gain). The raw t/s collapse is an isolated system anomaly on 2 of 16 cases (L07/L08@ctx32k: decode 3-4x slower, free RAM below 4 GB, GPU power collapsed to 81W vs 135W at equal or higher clock -- a transport-stall signature, not thermal), not isolated experimentally. Depurated t/s is 29.04 (+1.3%, within single-replica noise) but depurated acceptance stays at 0.7797, still below M1 -- the decision does not change even in the most favorable case. Fingerprints 18/18 identical to M1. M5 not run: neither trigger condition met. New risk R-RAM: with the MTP head and 32k context, minimum free RAM during a run must be logged in every future preset; a cell with a minimum below 4 GB is not a clean speed measurement until R-RAM is falsified or confirmed in isolation.
